chunks: It is narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding two men who agreed upon two just individuals and appointed them between themselves concerning a judgment in which a dispute had occurred between them, and they were satisfied with the two just individuals, but the two just individuals then differed between themselves: upon whose statement is the judgment to proceed?

He عليه السلام said: "One should look to the one who is more learned in fiqh, more knowledgeable of our hadith, and more scrupulous; then his judgment is to be carried out, and no attention is to be paid to the other."

key_terms.أَفْقَهِهِمَا: the one more knowledgeable in fiqh and legal understanding
key_terms.أَوْرَعِهِمَا: the one more scrupulous and cautious in religion
key_terms.بِأَحَادِيثِنَا: with respect to the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.حُكْمٍ: a legal judgment or decision in a dispute
key_terms.خِلَافٌ: a disagreement or dispute between parties
key_terms.عَدْلَيْنِ: two just individuals appointed to judge or arbitrate
key_terms.فَيَنْفُذُ حُكْمُهُ: his judgment is to be executed and enforced

ai.seo_question: If two just arbiters disagree in judgment, whose ruling should be followed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for resolving disagreement between two mutually appointed just arbiters. When they differ, priority is given to the one who is stronger in fiqh, more knowledgeable of the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, and more scrupulous in religion. The narration highlights the role of scholarly merit and piety in judicial authority.
